body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

accept | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says stay in the light of his lantern and he will keep the mist off; the nearest site is any of the seven paths. Two short sentences.
at_doors | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim waits at the doors, lantern held to the seam, and asks if they are ready to go on with the beacons. Two short sentences.
site_crypts | yorgrim | weary | Yorgrim, vaguer now, says this is where Marius's beacon burned, a knight who rode a horse called Dawn. One or two short sentences.
site_gardens | yorgrim | sad | Yorgrim says here Lethica kept her beacon, and that she hid a kind face behind a mask. One or two short sentences.
site_potters | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says Jericho's beacon, among nameless graves, fitting for a man the children loved. One or two short sentences.
site_lanes | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says Briggsy's fire here, a pirate with a heart of gold, and he will not say how many rum bottles are buried. One or two short sentences.
site_mounds | yorgrim | sad | Yorgrim says Farryn's beacon, a satyr who loved a human, and that the trees here still remember her. One or two short sentences.
clan_scene | Narrator | - | The standing stones are cut with Orc names, hundreds of them, root to crown. One sentence.
clan_1 | yorgrim | weary | Yorgrim, slowly, says these are the names of the Shadestone Clan, his clan, which he led in a ritual that was a trick; their souls were annihilated. Three short sentences.
clan_2 | yorgrim | sad | Yorgrim says the stone chained to his back carries the same names; he drags it to atone. Two short sentences.
doors_open | yorgrim | weary | Yorgrim, fainter, lantern small, says all six burn and the doors open; he talks less now and will not turn back. Three short sentences.
doors_isolde | Narrator | - | Yorgrim tells Isolde to stay and guard the door, and she lies down with a low whine, watching him go. One or two sentences.
isolde_door | Narrator | - | A black hound with bright white eyes holds a hooded lantern in her mouth and stands against the seam of the great doors, hackles up. One or two sentences.
isolde_hand | Narrator | - | The hound sniffs the offered hand and licks it once, then goes back to guarding the seam. One sentence.
isolde_calm | Narrator | - | The hound's hackles ease; she watches the party the way a guard watches a friend. One sentence.
isolde_fades | Narrator | - | Isolde, alone at the doors too long, flickers; her lantern gutters out, and she is gone; mist pours from the seam. Two sentences.
isolde_farewell | Narrator | - | Isolde lies by the doors under six burning sconces, then rises and turns toward the Shadestone stones as if to say follow. Two sentences.
isolde_rest | Narrator | - | At the Shadestone stones the hound lies down in the azure light and, for the first time, sleeps. One sentence.
crypt_study | Narrator | - | A crypt wall is worked with suns and roses; the family's crest. One sentence.
crypt_study_ok | Narrator | - | The suns and roses are Marius's family's, and they mark the crypt on the east of the courtyard. One or two sentences.
crypt_study_plain | Narrator | - | The carvings are fine work and tell the party nothing certain. One sentence.
crypt_door | Narrator | - | The crypt door is sealed with a basin at its foot; a blood tithe will open it. One sentence.
crypt_door2 | Narrator | - | The crypt door is sealed with a basin at its foot; a blood tithe will open it. One sentence.
crypt_bats_ok | Narrator | - | Bats burst out of the opened crypt and the party ducks them; the chamber beyond is empty and wrong. One or two sentences.
crypt_bats_fail | Narrator | - | Bats burst out of the crypt in a screaming cloud and bite. One sentence.
crypt_empty | yorgrim | neutral | Yorgrim says this is not the one, and something in the courtyard has stirred at the noise. Two short sentences.
crypt_door3 | Narrator | - | The crypt door is sealed with a basin at its foot; the suns and roses over it are the ones from the wall. One sentence.
crypt_right_hint | Narrator | - | This is the crypt the carvings pointed to. One short sentence.
crypt_right_ok | Narrator | - | Bats burst out; the party ducks them and the stair down is open. One sentence.
crypt_right_fail | Narrator | - | Bats burst out in a screaming cloud and bite as the stair opens. One sentence.
rose_take | Narrator | - | On a sarcophagus lid lies a dried red rose, light as paper, and the party takes it. One sentence.
fountain | Narrator | - | A wishing fountain burbles in the rain, coins gleaming in the basin. One sentence.
fountain_study | Narrator | - | A coin given blesses; a coin taken curses. Both last a few hours. One or two sentences.
fountain_plain | Narrator | - | The water keeps its secret. One short sentence.
result:
accept: Stay inside the pale ring of my lantern and the mist will keep its distance. Any of the seven iron paths leads to a dark beacon.
at_doors: The mist presses hard against the iron seam tonight. Tell me when you are ready to walk the paths and wake the beacons.
site_crypts: Marius kept his beacon burning above these old stones. He was a morning knight who rode a white horse named Dawn.
site_gardens: Lethica tended her pale fire among these wet yews. She wore a cold owl mask to hide a gentle face.
site_potters: Jericho lit his fire here among the nameless clay mounds. It suited a straw man who only wished to make the village children laugh.
site_lanes: Briggsy kept his watch along this crooked lane, a loud pirate with a heart of gold. I will not say how many rum bottles he buried under the sod.
site_mounds: Farryn raised her fire upon this green mound, a satyr who gave her heart to a mortal woman. The twisted roots beneath our boots still remember her song.
clan_scene: Tall standing stones rise from the wet heather, their grey faces chiselled from root to crown with hundreds of orcish names.
clan_1: These are the names of the Shadestone Clan, my blood and my charge. Our chieftain gave me a ritual, and I led them all to the knife. The dark took their souls and left not even ash.
clan_2: The granite slab chained across my shoulders bears every one of those same names. I drag their weight through the fog so the dead know I have not forgotten.
doors_open: Six pale fires burn again and the great iron doors unlatch. My lantern grows dim and my voice is nearly spent. I will not turn back from the stair below.
doors_isolde: Yorgrim lays two heavy fingers on Isolde's brow and bids her guard the threshold. The black hound sinks onto the cold flagstones with a low whine, her white eyes fixed on his fading back.
isolde_door: A spectral black hound stands braced against the seam of the great iron doors, hackles raised and bright white eyes unblinking. Between her jaws she grips the brass ring of a hooded lantern.
isolde_hand: The hound sniffs your outstretched knuckles and gives your skin one cool, rough lick before turning back to watch the iron seam.
isolde_calm: The bristle along the hound's dark spine smooths flat, and she watches you with the quiet steadiness of a sentry who knows a friend.
isolde_fades: Left too long at her post, Isolde thins like smoke until her hooded lantern gutters out and vanishes. Grave mist immediately hisses through the unguarded iron seam.
isolde_farewell: Under the steady glow of the six burning sconces, Isolde rises from the threshold and shakes the damp from her coat. She turns toward the carved stones of the Shadestone Clan and looks back once, waiting for you to follow.
isolde_rest: Beneath the standing stones the black hound curls into the cool azure light, lowers her muzzle onto her paws, and finally sleeps.
crypt_study: Across the damp limestone wall, a mason has carved a family crest of rising suns intertwined with briar roses.
crypt_study_ok: Those carved suns and briar roses belong to the house of Sir Marius Renathyr. Their stems point toward the weathered crypt on the eastern edge of the courtyard.
crypt_study_plain: The chiselled suns and roses are fine old masonry, though their meaning beneath the lichen remains uncertain to you.
crypt_door: A dry stone basin sits at the foot of the sealed crypt door, stained brown where a tithe of warm blood will unbar the lock.
crypt_door2: Another sealed stone door waits behind a dry offering basin at its threshold, hungry for a fresh drop of blood to release the bolt.
crypt_bats_ok: Leathery wings erupt from the open doorway, and you duck low as the cold draft washes over your necks. Beyond the threshold lies only a hollow, dust-choked vault that feels entirely wrong.
crypt_bats_fail: A screaming cloud of bats pours from the dark doorway, tearing at your faces with needle teeth and hooked claws.
crypt_empty: This vault holds only dust, not the knight we seek. Keep your blades drawn, for the racket has woken something out in the fog.
crypt_door3: A dry blood basin rests at the foot of this sealed door, crowned by the very same suns and briar roses carved upon the courtyard wall.
crypt_right_hint: Here stands the eastern crypt that the carved roses promised.
crypt_right_ok: Bats burst from the unsealed arch as you duck beneath their frantic wings, leaving the stone stair into the dark wide open.
crypt_right_fail: A shrieking swarm of bats explodes from the unsealed arch, biting at your bare skin as the stone stair yawns open below.
rose_take: Upon the cold sarcophagus lid rests a dried red rose as weightless as ash paper, and you slip its brittle stem into your pack.
fountain: Cold rain patters into a mossy wishing fountain where tarnished silver and copper coins gleam beneath the bubbling dark water.
fountain_study: Old churchyard custom clings to the cold basin: a coin dropped in grants a modest blessing, while a coin fished out invites a spiteful curse. Either mark will fade before a few hours pass.
fountain_plain: The dark water burbles over the old coins and keeps its secret.
